---

## Summary

I've added a full ML.NET-based ticket classifier to the .NET 10 Web API:

**Files created/modified:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `TicketClassifier.csproj` | Added `Microsoft.ML` 4.0.2 package |
| `Program.cs` | Registers `TicketClassifierService` as singleton |
| `Models/TicketData.cs` | ML.NET data model + prediction class |
| `Models/TicketRequest.cs` | API DTOs (request/response/metrics) |
| `Services/TicketClassifierService.cs` | Model training, evaluation & prediction |
| `Controllers/TicketController.cs` | REST endpoints |

**Pipeline:** Text featurization (Subject + Description) → Concatenate with Priority → Normalize → SDCA Maximum Entropy multiclass classifier

**Endpoints:**

```
POST /api/ticket/predict  → {"subject","description","priority"} → predicted category + confidence scores
GET  /api/ticket/metrics  → macroAccuracy, microAccuracy, logLoss, logLossReduction
```

**Test results:**
```json
// POST /api/ticket/predict
{ "predictedCategory": "Billing", "confidence": { "Technical": 0.03, "Billing": 0.93, "General": 0.04 } }

// GET /api/ticket/metrics
{ "macroAccuracy": 1.0, "microAccuracy": 1.0, "logLoss": 0.0002, "logLossReduction": 0.9998 }
```

> Note: Metrics show 100% accuracy because evaluation is on training data (only 6 samples). In production, use a larger dataset with train/test split or cross-validation.
